title: Choose the visual world for the Folio site
question: The roll assigned Attract Mode. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Attract Mode
options.lineage: arcade cabinets: backlit marquee, bezel art, attract loop, and the operator manual in the coin door
options.thesis: The landing page is the cabinet's attract loop; the docs are its operator manual.
options.viewport: A marquee band with FOLIO at full width in crisp vector type, the screen below cycling the real showcase videos, and a control-panel row whose big round START button is Hello world.
options.risk: Drifts toward the near-black neon arcade cliche if the side-art colours are timid; pixel fonts are out because they contradict the sharp-at-any-scale claim.

raised.raise: The marquee word repeats at five scales from one outline, proving the distance-field claim inside the hero rather than stating it.
The docs index is a row of identical cabinet-door modules, one per section, read by sweeping the row.
Total ink discipline: three side-art colours plus black and paper, each with one job (red action, yellow trap, blue link).
Solid red is reserved for the one decisive beat per page: START on the landing, the RCSS-is-not-CSS warning in docs.

options.label: The Instruction Booklet
options.lineage: staple-bound game manuals from the cartridge and jewel-case era
options.thesis: Folio's docs as the booklet in the box: controls diagram, numbered callouts, two-column spreads.
options.viewport: A cover spread: the Folio icon as box art, a controls diagram whose callouts point at Studio, markup and the world, and Getting started as page 2.
options.risk: The most familiar reading of game documentation; booklet stock edges toward the warm-paper default.

options.label: Field Specimen
options.thesis: A type specimen that toggles bitmap atlas versus distance field: Folio's mechanism as the page's honest state.
options.viewport: FOLIO at poster scale, the word repeated at five sizes down the margin; a switch flips the ladder between per-size bitmaps and one sharp field.
options.case: Wins product clarity outright; loses audience identification, game developers read it as a design-school poster.
options.risk: Bitmap display type fights the never-pixelated claim unless the bitmap side stays strictly the counter-example.

options.label: Riso Zine
options.thesis: Docs printed as a two-ink zine.
options.viewport: A misregistered two-ink cover with an index rail.
options.case: Loses both axes: misregistration argues against a crispness product.
options.kept: Total ink discipline: three colours, one job each.

options.label: Meter Bridge
options.viewport: A row of meters, one per doc section.
options.case: Loses both axes: the audio desk has no tie to game UI.
options.kept: Identical repeated modules as the index's ruler.

options.label: Deep Dive
options.thesis: Docs as a descent from surface to depth.
options.viewport: A vertical depth axis with sections as dive stages.
options.kept: One vertical axis ruling the reading order.

options.label: Chromatophore Skin
options.viewport: Skin patterns travelling under the headline.
options.kept: Surface-as-display, already the product's own claim.

options.label: Manga Page
options.viewport: A page of panels with the hero breaking the gutter.
options.kept: Solid fill reserved for the single decisive beat.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean developer-docs site: hero, feature grid, left sidebar, right table of contents.
canonCard.viewport: Headline, subcopy, Get started button beside a Studio screenshot.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other docs site by design.
